**Last Updated: July 28, 2026**

> The WSL2 dev-environment showcase that briefly replaced this file lives at [docs/wsl2-environment.md](docs/wsl2-environment.md).

A living list of what's done and what's left on this fork. This is a self-hosted-only fork of Coolify — the goal is a clean, no-frills, enterprise-friendly self-hosted deployment platform with no billing/marketing surface area.

## At a glance

This file is long and detailed on purpose — every claim below is backed by evidence (line numbers, exact commands, verification steps), not just asserted. That detail is useful if you want to check a specific claim, but it's not built for skimming, so here's the skim version first.

**Done, in full:**

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Livewire→React migration | 84/84 pages, complete 2026-07-14 — see "Livewire → React/Inertia migration" below |
| PHPStan baseline hardening | 1,306 → 60, 65 phases — see "PHPStan baseline reductions" below |
| De-commercialization | Billing/Stripe fully removed |
| Security hardening | CodeQL + Psalm, 11 real CVEs patched, 2 real findings fixed — see "GitHub repo-level security features" below |
| Laravel backend audit | Team-scoping, Sanctum tokens, cross-device reachability — see "Laravel backend improvements" below |

**Actually still open, right now:** 7 items — see the overview table at the top of **Still to do** below.

If you only read one section of this file, read this one and that table — everything else is the evidence trail behind them.

### PHPStan baseline milestones

Every phase touched the baseline, but only these actually found something — a real, previously-invisible bug, or a structural fix big enough to collapse dozens of duplicate entries at once. Everything else was routine typing; this table is the "what actually mattered" subset of the full phase table above.

| Phase | Commit | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | `ac32869a0` | Largest single-phase baseline drop of the whole initiative (1609 → 1323, −286): typing 6 widely-shared traits (`HasStandaloneDatabaseCommon`, `HasSafeStringAttribute` ×18 consumers, etc.) collapsed dozens of duplicate per-consumer entries into one. |
| 9 | `8a4b0d1d2` | Largest drop by absolute count (1244 → 1062, −182). Real bug fixed: a missing guard before calling `githubApi()` on an unsupported source-provider type now fails gracefully instead of type-erroring. |
| 11 | `a0d9e5710` | Real bug fixed: `envStore()`/`envUpdate()` now return a graceful error/404 when a resource has no `environment_variables()` relation, instead of a fatal method-call-on-generic-`Model` error PHPStan's typing had been masking. |
| 13 | `0a9d13249` | Real fatal bug: `customizeName()` and the `mountPath()`/`hostPath()` setters read `Stringable`'s **protected** `$value` property directly from an unrelated class — every call would have thrown a fatal `Error`. Fixed with the public `->toString()`. |
| 22 | — | Real bug fixed, TDD'd: `EmailChannel::send()` crashed with `strtolower(): ... null given` on a nullable `smtp_encryption` column — every sibling `smtp_*` field already null-coalesced, this one didn't. |
| 25 | `7c5263640` | 2 real bugs, both TDD'd: `isConfigurationChanged()` hashed full model instances instead of `pluck('value')`, making the "sorted for determinism" config hash actually order-dependent; and `ServiceExtraFieldsResolver`'s `$SERVICE_*` closures never captured `$service` and read a protected `Stringable::$value` — would fatal the instant a field value started with `$SERVICE_`. |
| 26 | `47bd8b8f6` | Real bug fixed, TDD'd: neither `ServiceApplication` nor `ServiceDatabase` cast `is_log_drain_enabled` to boolean — a fresh-from-DB instance returned SQLite's raw `int(1)`/`int(0)`, and declaring the accessor `: bool` would have thrown under `strict_types=1`. |
| 30 | `eb3c1cafa` | Real bug fixed: `Team::sources()`'s `Collection<GithubApp>::merge(Collection<GitlabApp>)` used the wrong `Collection` class (Eloquent's model-invariant one instead of `Illuminate\Support\Collection`) — found twice, independently, once in `sources()` and once in a `deleting` event closure. |
| 33 | `b6443e257` | 2 real bugs: a permanently-dead SSL-cert-param branch on 3 database engines that never actually had an `ssl_mode` column; and `databaseType()` was `public` instead of `protected`, so Larastan couldn't recognize it as a valid computed Attribute property despite working fine at runtime. |
| 41 | `91f88653b` | 2 real bugs, TDD'd: `loadComposeFile()`'s stale-domain pruning always took its truthy branch (a `Collection` is always truthy in PHP) so `docker_compose_domains` could get permanently stuck at `"[]"` instead of reverting to `null`; and 4 call sites string-compared `getMorphClass()` instead of using `instanceof`, blocking type narrowing. |
| 42 | `6a084c314` | Real fatal-shaped bug, TDD'd: `Server::status()` called the `services()` relation **method** directly in a `foreach` instead of `->get()`-ing it first — a relation builder isn't `Traversable`, so the loop body silently never executed, and a downed server's Service-based resources never got marked `'exited'`. |
| 45 | `2298b4243` | Real bug fixed, TDD'd: `forceDeployService()` tried to mark stuck activities as errored via `$activity->properties->status = ...` — `properties` is a `Collection`-cast attribute, so this set a dynamic property on the Collection object itself and never persisted. Fixed by reassigning the attribute via `->put()`. |
| 50 | `3cfe828de` | Structural fix, largest drop since Phase 6 (361 → 225, −136): converted `App\Contracts\StandaloneDatabaseInstance` from a plain interface to an abstract class, since Larastan never resolves PHPDoc through an interface. Migrated all 8 database engines and 27 consuming files; caught a real runtime `TypeError` in a test fixture still typed against the deleted interface (63 failing tests surfaced it immediately). |
| 52 | `d082d1ae0` | Real dead code removed: `SslCertificate`'s `application()`/`service()`/`database()` relation methods were unused everywhere — every real caller reads the raw `resource_type`/`resource_id` columns directly — so they were deleted rather than typed. |
| 56 | `103d4e01c` | The most severe bug found this session, TDD'd: `ServerLimitCheckJob::handle()` read `$this->team->limits`, a property that has never existed on `Team` (the real column is `custom_server_limit`) — Eloquent's magic getter silently returned `null`, and PHP's `-` operator treated it as `0`, so **every team with at least one server would have had all of them force-disabled** on every run. The job is never actually dispatched anywhere in the current codebase (confirmed via grep), so it never fired in production — but the fix has lasting value if it's ever wired up. |
| 60 | `1d9233c7a` | 2 real bugs: `CleanupStuckedResources.php` called the `destination()` relation **method** instead of the property on 4 of 7 engine blocks, so an orphaned-destination cleanup branch could never fire for those engines (masked by an adjacent, differently-worded check catching the same case); and `StandaloneRedisFactory` still wrote a `redis_password` column a migration had dropped over a year earlier — `StandaloneRedis::factory()->create()` had been silently broken the whole time, never exercised by any existing test. |
| 64 | `d8c4ccb25` | Real, TDD'd production bug: `ApplicationPreview::generate_preview_fqdn_compose()` passed a nullable `docker_compose_domains` column straight into `json_decode()` with no null guard — under this codebase's `strict_types=1`, the very first preview-fqdn generation for any fresh docker-compose application would crash before generating a single domain, across all 6 real call sites. |

**What's left in the 60-entry baseline (2026-07-19 audit, updated after Phase 65):** all 60 are confirmed PHPStan/Larastan false positives, individually verified, not assumed — nothing neglected.

| Category | Entries | Why it's a false positive |
|---|---|---|
| Trait per-class-context artifact | 27 (`instanceof.alwaysFalse` ×12, `catch.neverThrown` ×11, `booleanOr.alwaysFalse` ×3, +1) | `ClearsGlobalSearchCache.php` is shared by 13 models — PHPStan analyzes the trait once per consuming class with `$this` narrowed to that concrete type, so a check relevant to a *different* consumer gets flagged "always false" even though the trait needs that branch for its other real consumers. |
| `Illuminate\Support\Collection`'s non-covariant `TValue` template | 11 (`return.type` ×10, `argument.type` ×1) | `dumpType()` (Phase 62) confirmed the declared and actual shapes print as structurally identical, yet PHPStan still rejects it — a documented upstream limitation, not fixable without loosening real types. Mostly `SettingsScheduledJobsController.php` + `TerminalController::getAllActiveContainers()`. |
| Engine-specific dynamic column access | 11 (`property.notFound`) | `StandaloneDatabaseInstance::$mariadb_database`/`$mysql_database`/`$postgres_db`/`$enable_ssl`/`$ssl_mode` etc. — the base/abstract type doesn't declare every engine's specific columns, but the concrete runtime subclass always does. Established Phase 50/52. |
| Magic-property "remembering" artifact | 3 (`identical.alwaysFalse`) | `ManagesApiResourceStorages.php:410` — `dumpType()` confirmed PHPStan's own internal type-flow computes `*NEVER*` for `$request->type` there, from an interaction between an earlier ternary and a later `$request->has()` call. | 2026-07-22 | Dev-environment infra, not app code, but tracked here since it's a real fix, not just documentation: the Docker Desktop/WSL2 post-reboot race (`DEVELOPING_IN_CONTAINERS_WINDOWS.md`'s documented `coolify` empty-mount issue) turned out to not be fully solved by the existing `autoheal` sidecar. Tested against two real reboots — including one *after* enabling Docker Desktop's "start on sign-in" setting, which fixes a different problem (Docker not running yet) but not this one. Both times, the race hit multiple containers at once, including `coolify-autoheal` itself (exited `127`) plus `mailpit`/`minio`/`vite`/`testing-host` — none of which had any `restart:` policy set at all, a real silent gap independent of this specific bug. Fixed, two parts: (1) `restart: unless-stopped` added to the 4 unprotected services; (2) `scripts/dev-up.sh`, a host-side detect-and-fix script — run once after logging back in following a reboot. A container-native auto-fix (`mount-doctor`, `restart: always`, no bind mount of its own besides the Docker socket) was built first, on the theory that a socket-only container would be immune to the race; a Windows Task Scheduler entry was considered and deliberately rejected in favor of it, for portability. A third real reboot disproved the theory: `mount-doctor` itself came up `Exited (127)`, alongside `coolify-autoheal`/`coolify-realtime`/`coolify-testing-host`. `docker inspect` on all four showed the real mechanism is broader than "directory mount attaches empty": *file* bind mounts (`docker.sock`, soketi's individual `.js` file mounts) fail OCI container-creation outright on reboot ("mounting a directory onto a file"), rather than merely attaching empty like directory mounts do — and `mount-doctor` needs `docker.sock` to do anything, so it's a victim of the exact failure it exists to repair. Nothing running inside a container can recover from a failure that happens before that container can be created; `mount-doctor` was removed, and `dev-up.sh` (host-side, immune to this class of race) is the real fix. A follow-up attempt to synthetically test the failure path (hiding `artisan` via `docker exec`) was itself a mistake — bind mounts have no separate container-side copy, so it moved the real host file; caught immediately, fully restored, confirmed byte-identical via `git status`. See issue #45. |

This silently broke `ServerConnectionCheckJob`'s Docker-availability check, cascading into `Server::isFunctional()` returning false and every docker-cleanup run being skipped. A plain `docker restart coolify-testing-host` fixed it immediately; re-dispatching `ServerConnectionCheckJob` synced `is_usable` back to `true`. `scripts/dev-up.sh` updated to add a functional check specifically for this container — verifying `docker version`'s Server block is non-null, not just that container status is `running`, since "running" alone wasn't sufficient evidence the mount had actually reconnected. See `DEVELOPING_IN_CONTAINERS_WINDOWS.md`'s reboot-race section. |

### Laravel backend improvements

Not related to the Livewire→React migration — a separate, dedicated backend-quality pass, prompted by the user asking for a general Laravel-improvement audit of the repo (audited 2026-07-15). Findings are evidence-based (line/method counts, live `pg_indexes` queries, actual config values); a few initial suspicions (mass-assignment protection, `APP_DEBUG` defaulting unsafe in production, missing API rate limiting) were investigated and ruled out as non-issues. One further finding from this audit is deliberately left open, not a bug — see "Laravel backend improvements — still open" in **Still to do**.

| Item | Date | Finding & fix |
|---|---|---|
| PHPStan baseline: 1,306 → 60 suppressed errors | — | 65 phases/commits, all 60 remaining entries confirmed as analysis-tool limitations — see "PHPStan baseline reductions" above, not duplicated here. |
| `Application`/`Service` team-scoping: 3-hop relation join, not indexed | 2026-07-19 | `whereRelation('environment.project.team', ...)` on every team-scoped query, unlike `Server`/`Project`'s direct indexed `team_id`. Added an indexed `team_id` column to both tables + backfill + a `saving()` sync hook; converted 18 more `Service::whereRelation(...)` call sites too. `ServiceApplication`/`ServiceDatabase`/the 8 standalone-database models have the same pattern one level deeper — deliberately out of scope (separate future ticket). One known, deliberately-unfixed edge case: the sync hook doesn't fire if a `Project`'s `team_id` changes after creation (confirmed no real code path does this today). |

| 2026-07-23 | Application Deployment smoke test, continued and closed out: with both prior crashes fixed, a real deployment against the seeded dev server now **actually succeeds end-to-end** (real `docker build`, real rolling update, real container started) — confirmed via Playwright watching the real deployment log stream. Confirmed both live-update checklist items directly, watching the DOM change with zero manual refreshes of any kind: the Deployment Show page's own 2s poll took a fresh deployment from "In Progress" to "Finished" entirely on its own; the Deployment Index page's 5s poll did the same for its deployment list. Deploy, Redeploy, Restart, Stop, and Force Deploy (without cache) were each individually triggered live and confirmed to actually do the real thing (real container stop/start, real status transitions) — not just render the right button. **While testing Stop, found and fixed a much bigger, systemic bug**: `composer.json`'s `autoload-dev.files` unconditionally loaded 3 test-fake files (`tests/Support/Fakes/{action_remote_process_overrides,database_action_overrides,model_remote_process_overrides}.php`) into *every* PHP process in this dev environment, not just test runs — since dev dependencies (and therefore `autoload-dev`) are always active locally (`APP_ENV=local`, distinct from `phpunit.xml`'s `APP_ENV=testing`). These files intentionally declare same-named functions inside real app namespaces (`App\Actions\Application`, `App\Actions\Database`, `App\Models`) so PHP's namespace-resolution rules make unqualified calls resolve to the fake instead of the real global implementation — a legitimate test-double trick, but only if scoped to actual test execution, which it wasn't. Confirmed impact: clicking Stop crashed with "Typed static property `Tests\Support\Fakes\RemoteProcessFake::$containers` must not be accessed before initialization," reachable from `StopApplication`, `StopApplicationOneServer`, and `CleanupPreviewDeployment` — real, user-facing, silently broken in every real dev request the whole time these fakes existed. Worse: the `App\Actions\Database` override shadows 9 real functions this way, including `isDev()` and `convertDockerRunToCompose()` — meaning this same session's earlier `convertDockerRunToCompose()` null-guard fix (see the entry above) was being silently bypassed for any code in that namespace, since real calls never reached the fixed implementation at all. Applied the proper fix, not a band-aid: removed all 3 files from `composer.json`'s `autoload-dev.files` (matching what 2 of the 3 files' own doc comments already said should happen — the loading-mechanism documentation itself was stale/wrong), ran `composer dump-autoload`, then added explicit `require_once` to the 16 real test files that had been silently relying on the eager load — centralized into the 2 shared test traits (`InteractsWithDatabaseActions`, `InteractsWithStartDatabaseProxy`) where 8 of those files already shared one, rather than duplicating the `require_once` across each individually. Full Pest suite (1245/1245), Pint, PHPStan, and `composer validate` all clean after. One operational gotcha worth knowing: a *running* Horizon worker doesn't pick up an autoloader fix just from `composer dump-autoload` or even `horizon:terminate` — PHP function definitions are permanent for a process's lifetime, and Horizon's worker processes are forked from (not freshly exec'd from) an already-running master, so the master process itself has to be killed and let `s6-supervise` restart it fresh before real requests stop hitting the stale, pre-fix function table. See issue #21. |

Worse in the preview scope: `EnvironmentVariable::booted()`'s own `created()` hook auto-mirrors every new non-preview var into a preview copy too, so the default seed alone produced *both* a non-preview and a preview row before either cloning loop even ran, and the existing preview-clone loop had the identical blind-insert problem stacked on top. New Pest test in `ProjectApplicationConfigurationTabsTest.php`, TDD-proved via `git stash`. Duplicate-name rejection, both clone destinations, tag/env-var carry-over, and the volume-data checkbox all confirmed correct afterward. **Found and cleaned up on teardown, not a bug**: `Project`/`Environment` deletion doesn't cascade to their applications/databases (2 orphaned rows found and removed) — same class of gap as the destination-cleanup finding earlier in this smoke-test pass. Ruled out, with direct evidence, every repo-side explanation before considering it external: `.github/workflows/quality.yml` byte-identical between local and the exact failing commit on GitHub (fetched via the raw-content API), valid YAML, repo public with unlimited Actions minutes, Actions permissions unrestricted, no stuck concurrency lock (reran the same failed run 3 times over several minutes, identical failure each time), no queue/capacity exhaustion from those reruns (nothing else stuck), not tied to one specific run object (a genuinely fresh push produced a new run that failed the same way). **Made the diagnosis harder than it needed to be**: reran the same workflow repeatedly while both `quality.yml` and `codeql.yml` have `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` on the ref, so each new attempt was likely cancelling the previous one before it could finish — confirmed directly when a CodeQL run's own log showed `Error: The operation was canceled.` 42 queries into real evaluation, not an instant parse-time rejection. Real lesson, worth keeping: don't rapid-fire reruns/pushes against a `cancel-in-progress` workflow while diagnosing it — each attempt can cancel the last, making a transient issue look like a persistent, reproducible break and burning real time chasing what's actually your own interference. Stopped touching it, waited, and the very next real push (the `Project/Database/Backup/Index.test.jsx` commit) ran clean end-to-end with zero intervention: Quality, CodeQL, and Pages all green — confirmed independently two ways, not just taken on faith: directly in the GitHub UI (watched live) and via `gh run list`/`gh api`, matching. Not written up as a third incident report — unlike the two in `docs/incident.md`, there's no confirmed root cause pinned to this repo's own code/config and no code fix, just an external hiccup that resolved once nothing further disturbed it, with real application behavior unaffected throughout. GitHub's own status page showed no listed incident at any point during this. |
| 2026-07-25 | CI infra, not app code, but tracked here since it's a real, root-caused, verified fix: the Actions "Caches" page showed 9.94 of a 10GB budget in use across 96 entries. 95 were `codeql-trap-1-2.26.1-javascript-{commit-sha}` caches, ~108MB each, one per commit — every one keyed uniquely to its own SHA, so none were ever restored as a hit by a later run, just a fresh write-and-discard on every push. The two caches that actually matter for CI speed (`composer-*`, `node-cache-*-yarn-*`) were tiny by comparison and correctly being reused. Root cause confirmed against a matching, already-known upstream issue: `github/codeql-action#2030`, "TRAP caching causes GitHub Actions Cache to churn," most visible on repos with no long-lived base commit for the cache key to reuse against. Fixed by adding `trap-caching: false` to `codeql.yml`'s `Initialize CodeQL` step, and deleted all 94 stale `codeql-trap-*` entries directly via the Actions cache API rather than waiting for slow LRU eviction — safe outright, since none had ever been restored and none ever would be again. Verified against the real cache list, not just the account-level usage summary stat (confirmed lagging behind real deletes by several minutes): total usage dropped from 10.68GB across 96 entries to 0.69GB across 3, leaving exactly the caches that are actually reused. | 2026-07-25 | Dependabot found a real high-severity PostCSS vulnerability (`GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849`, [alert #2](https://github.com/Terrence721/coolify-full/security/dependabot/2)) and auto-opened PR #53 (8.5.16 → 8.5.18): PostCSS auto-loads a "previous source map" from a `/*# sourceMappingURL=... */` comment inside parsed CSS, and the path join doesn't sandbox `../` traversal — a crafted comment can read an arbitrary `.map` file off disk, or an absolute path verbatim if `opts.from` isn't set. Checked reachability before merging rather than trusting the advisory blindly, same discipline as the `ws` DoS fix (issue #50): `postcss` is a direct dependency, but its only invocation anywhere in this repo is `postcss.config.cjs` via `@tailwindcss/postcss` for Vite's build-time CSS pipeline — a full grep of `app/`/`resources/` found zero direct `require`/`import` of it. It only ever parses this repo's own developer-authored CSS at build time; unlike `ws`, there's no runtime path where attacker-supplied CSS reaches it, so this one isn't currently exploitable in this app's actual usage. Merged anyway (squash, all 7 CI checks green first) since it's a free, patch-only bump with zero functional risk. Verified the fix is actually live, not just merged on GitHub: `docker exec coolify-vite yarn install --frozen-lockfile` picked up 8.5.18, confirmed in `node_modules/postcss/package.json`, and a real `yarn build` completed cleanly against the new version. | 2026-07-25 | Found by noticing a real discrepancy in the Security tab, not by trusting its own summary: 3 closed Dependabot alerts, but only 2 had a PR reference — `brace-expansion` (`GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg`/`CVE-2026-14257`, high, [alert #3](https://github.com/Terrence721/coolify-full/security/dependabot/3)) didn't. Its `created_at` and `auto_dismissed_at` are the exact same timestamp — a system dismissal, not a human one, most likely because the vulnerable version is several levels deep in the tree with nothing in our own `package.json` for Dependabot to bump directly, so it gave up rather than leaving an unfixable-by-PR alert open. The vulnerable version was still genuinely resolved in the committed `yarn.lock` (`brace-expansion@^5.0.5` → `5.0.7`, exactly the top of the vulnerable range) — confirmed directly rather than trusting the alert's closed status. The bug itself: `expand()` bounds result *count* (`max`, default 100,000) but not result *length* — chaining brace groups stays under `max` while every result grows with the group count, exhausting memory with an uncatchable fatal V8 OOM that `try/catch` can't stop. Reachability: comes in via `eslint`'s own `minimatch` dependency (`yarn why` confirms), pure dev-tooling, not reachable at runtime — same category as the PostCSS finding, fixed anyway since it's free and correct. Dependabot couldn't open a PR for this one itself, so fixed manually with a scoped Yarn `resolutions` override in `package.json` targeting the exact nested path, not a blanket override — there's a second, unrelated `brace-expansion@1.1.16` elsewhere in the tree (a different major version line via `eslint-plugin-react`'s own older `minimatch`) that a blanket override would have forced onto 5.0.8 too, for zero benefit since it's already outside the vulnerable range. Took 3 attempts to get the resolution syntax right, each verified against the real `yarn.lock`/`yarn why` output rather than trusted from `yarn install`'s exit status alone: an npm-overrides-style key errored outright (invalid Yarn Classic syntax), a single-level nested path silently resolved to the wrong location (left `5.0.7` still actually hoisted, just added a dead unused `5.0.8` entry), and the working form needed the full nested path from the direct dependency down through every intermediate package. Confirmed via `yarn why brace-expansion` that the real, in-use copy is `5.0.8`, not just that an entry exists somewhere in the lockfile. Full suites clean: `yarn lint` (the actual consumer) unaffected at the same 22-error baseline, Vitest 450/450, `yarn build` succeeds, `format:check` clean. See issue #55 (closed). |

| 2026-07-26 | Found and fixed live while manually clicking through the app (not via automated testing): all 9 error pages (`400`/`401`/`402`/`403`/`404`/`419`/`429`/`500`/`503`) served genuinely invalid HTML and forced the browser into Quirks Mode. Root cause: every view in `resources/views/errors/` did `@extends('layouts.base')` followed by raw, un-sectioned page content — but `layouts/base.blade.php`'s `<body>` is entirely self-contained inside `@section('body') ... @show` with no `@yield` for a child's content to land in. Blade only renders the *parent* layout after the *child* view's own script finishes, so the un-sectioned content printed to the output buffer immediately — before the parent's own `<!DOCTYPE html>` — putting real page content before the doctype in the final response. Confirmed directly, not just from reading the template: safely reproduced a real 419 (corrupted just the outgoing CSRF token on an isolated Playwright browser context, no shared session/DB state touched) and captured the actual raw response — bare `<div>`, no doctype nearby; live in a real browser, `document.compatMode` read `'BackCompat'` (quirks) and `document.doctype` was `null` before the fix. Every real working standalone page (`auth/login.blade.php` and siblings) instead uses the `<x-layout-simple>` component, which correctly threads content through a `{{ $slot }}` — the 9 error views were the only views in the app not using it. Fixed by converting all 9 to `<x-layout-simple>...</x-layout-simple>`. **Found a secondary issue while fixing**: 8 of the 9 views used `h-full` for vertical centering, which only resolves against an ancestor with a defined height, and nothing in the corrected component chain gives `<body>` one — content rendered top-anchored instead of centered once the doctype bug was fixed. `500.blade.php` (and the real `login.blade.php`) already used `min-h-screen` for the same effect; applied the same fix to the other 8. New test, `tests/v4/Feature/ErrorPageLayoutTest.php` (9 assertions, one per error code): renders each view directly and asserts the output starts with a real `<!doctype html>`; TDD-proved — failed on all 9 against the original code (`'<div class="fle'` instead of `'<!doctype html>'`), passes clean after the fix. Live re-verified afterward too: `document.compatMode` now `'CSS1Compat'`, real doctype present, centering visually restored. Full suite clean: 1,260 Pest (was 1,251 + 9 new), Pint, PHPStan 0 errors. | 2026-07-26 | Found live in a real browser session (not a synthetic repro): a genuine 419 on `/logout` after several real login/logout cycles. Root-caused: `AppLayout.jsx`'s sidebar Logout form reads its CSRF `_token` from `document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]')`, a `<meta>` tag Blade renders exactly once, on the initial full-document load — Inertia's client-side navigation never re-renders `<head>`, and a full-repo grep confirmed nothing anywhere ever updates that tag's value afterward. That token is therefore frozen in the DOM for the entire life of a browser tab, regardless of what happens to the live server session (login/logout elsewhere rotates and regenerates the session's real CSRF token via `session()->regenerate()`/`invalidate()`). A page resurrected from the browser's back/forward cache (bfcache) — a real, common outcome of hitting Back after a login/logout cycle — carries that same frozen, now-stale token, so submitting Logout from it gets rejected by CSRF verification before the app ever sees the request. Attempted to reproduce the exact trigger via Playwright (login → logout → login → browser Back) - headless Chromium re-fetched a fresh dashboard on back-navigation rather than serving a stale bfcache snapshot, so the precise trigger in a real browser (Edge, per the report) couldn't be pinned down further; the underlying staleness itself, however, was independently confirmed directly from the code and is real regardless of which exact DOM-caching mechanism resurrects it. Fixed with the standard mitigation for this whole bug class: a new `reloadOnBFCacheRestore()` (`resources/js/hooks/reloadOnBFCacheRestore.js`), wired into both JS entrypoints (`inertia-app.jsx` and `app.js`), listening for `pageshow` with `event.persisted === true` and forcing `window.location.reload()` - guaranteeing any bfcache-restored page immediately re-fetches a fresh document with a token that matches the live session, before the user could ever act on the stale one. 2 new tests (`reloadOnBFCacheRestore.test.jsx`), TDD-proved (temporarily short-circuited the `persisted` check, confirmed the test failed with the exact symptom, restored). Live-verified in a real Playwright browser session against the actual bundled app: a normal, non-persisted `pageshow` triggers zero reloads (no regression/reload-loop risk), while a genuinely `persisted: true` `pageshow` reliably triggers a real page reload. Full suite clean: 525 Vitest (52 suites, was 523/51), `format:check` clean, `yarn build` clean, ESLint unaffected (confirmed via `git stash` that the pre-existing baseline is actually 23 errors, not the 22 several earlier log entries cite - untouched either way). See issue #60 (closed). |

### Fresh-clone end-to-end boot test (deferred 2026-07-13 — destructive, run when losing dev data is acceptable)

The first-boot automation (`php artisan dev --init`) is covered by feature tests and an idempotent live run, but has **not** been proven with a true from-scratch boot the way a real cloner would experience it — doing so wipes every named volume (all dev projects/servers/applications, the dev database, backups, MinIO data). Steps, when ready:

```bash
# 0. Commit/push everything first. This destroys all local dev data.
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml down -v

# 1. Simulate a fresh cloner's .env (APP_KEY intentionally empty in the template)
cp .env.development.example .env

# 2. First boot — init runs composer install, migrate, dev --init automatically
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d

# 3. Wait for the app to report healthy, then verify
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml ps
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/health
```

Expected: `APP_KEY` now populated in `.env` (written by `key:generate` through the bind mount), login works at `http://localhost:8000` with `test@example.com` / `password`, and no `coolify-proxy` container yet (the app creates it at runtime — see `DEVELOPING_IN_CONTAINERS_WINDOWS.md` §2). Caveats: cached `coolify:dev`/`coolify-realtime:dev`/`coolify-testing-host:dev` images make this test skip the image-build path — to also prove a from-scratch **build**, remove those images first and expect the possible `NGINX_VERSION` pin issue documented in `docs/command.md`'s WSL2-migration section, step 6.

### Verification standing habit

- Every change in this repo is expected to go through: `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent`, `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`, `php artisan test --compact`, and `yarn build` before being considered done. See `docs/command.md` for the exact commands.
